Subject: Enterprise Access staging QA & implementation checklist

Hi Sara / BluePeak security team —

Thanks for the quick kickoff yesterday. To keep momentum we want to run a focused staging QA for SSO (SAML), SCIM provisioning, egress IP allowlist validation, and service-account provisioning. Please see the attached mutual action plan and the IP allowlist template to fill in your network contacts and IP ranges.

Ask list (short):
- SAML IdP metadata (XML) or metadata URL + preferred flow (SP-initiated or IdP-initiated)
- SCIM admin token or instructions for token exchange (we support bearer tokens delivered over an HTTPS POST to our staging endpoint)
- Completed ip-allowlist-template.csv with firewall owner and maintenance windows
- Names and intended scopes for any Redwood service accounts you want created in staging (we recommend least-privilege and a <team>-svc-<env> naming pattern)
- Any organisational policies (session timeouts, IP blocks) that could impact sign-on/testing

Timing: our staging cluster is available next week; propose a 60–90 minute QA window on Tue Apr 20 or Wed Apr 21. If you share available slots and the IP ranges we can pre-provision a temporary allowlist to avoid manual firewall changes during the test.

Attachments: MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN.xlsx (MAP), ip-allowlist-template.csv, sso-scim-implementation-deck.pdf

Note: Monica will own SCIM token exchange and Ben will own network verification / telemetry checks. I’ll coordinate the runbook and postmortem.

Thanks —
Mateo Alvarez

Hi all — quick technical clarifications from the SCIM/SSO side before we lock a slot.

1) SCIM token: preferred approach is a scoped bearer token posted to our staging token endpoint (https://staging-auth.redwood.com/scim/token). We can accept either a long-lived token for testing or a short-lived token exchanged using your token service; please indicate if your org requires IP-restricted keys.

2) SCIM base URL and attributes: our staging SCIM endpoint will be https://staging-scim.redwood.com/v2/Users. We support: userName, externalId, name.givenName, name.familyName, active, emails[type eq "work"]. We recommend doing a small batch (10–20 users) for the QA to validate create/update/delete.

3) SAML: We support both SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows. If you can provide the IdP metadata XML that’s fastest. Also include the NameID format you expect (email vs persistent).

4) IPs: for TCP egress we'll provide a short list of staging egress IPs and advise a 1-hour pre-allow period to confirm connectivity. If your firewall team requires CIDR blocks, use the attached template.

5) Service accounts: we will create one Redwood-managed service account in staging with delegated SCIM write scope and one for observability only. Please list the display names you want; keep to the pattern team-svc-staging for clarity.

I attached an edited copy of the IP template with the column for 'Firewall contact' filled — Ben will validate once you confirm.

If that all sounds good I can stand by for a Tue/Wed slot and prepare the SCIM test users.

Monica Patel
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com

- NameID: we use email as NameID by default
- SCIM token: we can generate a short-lived token and post it to your staging token endpoint; our security team would prefer the token be IP-restricted to our egress blocks (see below)
- IPs: our current outbound CIDRs are 198.51.100.0/24 and 203.0.113.0/28 — attaching a contact card for the firewall owner (Chris Nguyen) and maintenance window policy
- Service accounts: we'll request two: bluepeak-it-svc-staging (SCIM write) and bluepeak-monitor-svc (observability only).
